intro: Limassol learner drivers have more choice than ever in 2026, with top-rated schools spread across the city from Agios Athanasios to Mesa Geitonia.

schools.fdf86914ce3a03d1: Driving School Nikolas Papanikolaou sits at the top of the Limassol rankings with a perfect 5.0 rating from 527 reviews. Based on Ellis Lampeti 5 in Agios Athanasios, this school covers the full eastern side of the city and has easy access to the Yermasoyia test routes. Students praise the calm teaching style and the way lessons are tailored to each driver's pace. Theory help is offered alongside practical sessions, which helps first-time candidates pass the written test. The fleet is modern and well maintained. If you live near the Agios Athanasios roundabout, the highway exits, or the eastern suburbs, this school is a strong first choice for car licence training in 2026.
schools.f66ddc0f1c63e490: Driving School Limassol Cyprus Demetrakis, also known as Scholi Odigon Lemesos Kypros Dimitrakis, is based at Evkaf 15 in central Limassol. With 132 five-star reviews, it has built a reputation for patient instruction and high pass rates. The central location near the old town makes it easy for students from Kapsalos, Tsiflikoudia, and the port area to attend lessons after work. Demetrakis is known for explaining road signs and roundabout rules in plain language, which helps nervous drivers settle in quickly. The school handles both manual and automatic lessons. It is a strong pick for adults learning later in life and for tourists or expats who need clear English-language teaching.
schools.58ec62fc19444191: Nikolas Ioannides School of Motoring operates from Leontiou Center, Block C 171, in the heart of Limassol at postcode 3041. With 103 reviews and a 5.0 rating, the school is well known among students from the city centre and the Linopetra district. Lessons cover everything from basic clutch control to confident motorway driving on the A1. Instructors take time on parking drills, which is a common weak point in the practical test. The central base means lessons often include real urban traffic from day one, so students get used to busy junctions like Makariou Avenue and Spyrou Kyprianou. A solid choice for anyone wanting city-ready skills.
schools.44896ac8f737beb9: LDS is located on Agias Fylaxeos 162A in the 3083 district, close to one of the busiest commuter roads in Limassol. The school holds a perfect 5.0 rating from 15 reviews and has earned trust through steady, careful coaching. Agias Fylaxeos itself is a great training ground because it has every type of junction: traffic lights, mini roundabouts, pedestrian crossings, and bus lanes. Students who train with LDS get plenty of exposure to real driving conditions. The school is friendly to teenagers taking their first lessons at 17 and 18, and to working adults who need flexible afternoon and weekend slots. Pricing is fair and the lesson structure is clear.
schools.c5dc12dcbcf16180: Mr Driver is based at Petrou Tsirou 14B in the 3085 area, very close to the Linopetra interchange and the Limassol hospital. With a 5.0 rating from 9 reviews, this is a smaller school with a personal feel. Lessons often start with quiet residential streets in Agia Fyla before moving onto Petrou Tsirou and Franklin Roosevelt Avenue for heavier traffic practice. Mr Driver is a good fit for students who want one consistent instructor from first lesson to test day. The school helps with the theory test booking process and gives clear feedback after every drive. New drivers from the western neighbourhoods will find this location very convenient.
schools.96dce9ded26e8296: Andy's Driving School works out of Typaldou 18 in the 3081 postcode of Limassol, in the Agia Fyla area. With a 5.0 rating from 5 reviews, Andy's is a boutique school with a loyal student base. The area around Typaldou has a mix of narrow residential roads and wider connector streets, which gives learners early practice in lane discipline and judging gaps. Andy's is known for honest progress reports, so students know exactly when they are ready for the test. Lessons can be booked in both Greek and English. This is a good option for residents of Agia Fyla, Polemidia, and the western suburbs who prefer a small, friendly school over a large operation.
schools.36ee0bb7aad9398e: Scholi Odigon Koufallis is based on Agias Fylaxeos in the 3087 district and holds a 5.0 rating from 4 reviews. The Koufallis family name is well established in Limassol driving instruction, and the school passes on years of local knowledge in every lesson. Students get hands-on practice on Agias Fylaxeos, one of the most demanding roads in the city, plus quieter streets for hill starts and reversing drills. The school keeps class sizes small so each learner gets full attention. It is a sensible pick for students living between Agia Fyla and Polemidia who want a no-nonsense, traditional approach to learning to drive.
schools.ce144e9bfe6baca4: Leonidas Tsappas Driving School operates from Nikou Nikolaidi 3 in the 3065 postcode, close to the Limassol seafront and the Tsireion stadium area. With a 5.0 rating from 3 reviews, this school is a smaller name that delivers careful, patient instruction. The seafront location gives learners regular exposure to busy tourist traffic during summer months, which is great practice for handling unexpected pedestrian crossings and slow-moving vehicles. Leonidas Tsappas is known for working well with anxious learners and people who failed the test elsewhere and want a fresh start. The school can arrange test day support so candidates feel calm and prepared on the morning of the exam.
schools.9a3d2b24a913bf50: Maria's Driving School is located on Apostolou Vakalopoulou in Kato Polemidia, postcode 4152. With a 5.0 rating from 2 reviews, Maria's is one of the few female-led driving schools in Limassol, which many women learners find more comfortable, especially for their first lessons. Kato Polemidia has a useful mix of residential streets, school zones, and a quick connection to the Polemidia roundabout and the motorway. Lessons cover all the basics plus confidence-building drills for night driving and rainy conditions. Maria's is a strong pick for students living in Polemidia, Ypsonas, and the western edge of Limassol who want a calm, supportive learning environment.
schools.f7329b10d78e0778: Limassol Driving School Petros Eleftheriou is based at 1is Apriliou 39 in Mesa Geitonia, postcode 4003. With 397 reviews and a 4.9 rating, this is one of the most established names in the city. Mesa Geitonia sits right in the middle of Limassol, making the school easy to reach from almost any neighbourhood. Petros Eleftheriou runs a structured course with clear milestones, so students always know what skill comes next. The school handles a high volume of test candidates each month and knows the local examiner routes well. Strong fleet, experienced instructors, and a track record of pass results make this a reliable choice for first-time drivers and licence converters in 2026.

closing: Learning to drive in Limassol in 2026 is different from learning in any other Cyprus city. The coastal capital of the south has grown fast over the last decade, and the road network now mixes old narrow streets in the city centre with wide modern avenues and a busy motorway. Students need to be ready for all of it. Areas like Agios Athanasios, Mesa Geitonia, Agia Fyla, and Kato Polemidia each have their own driving character. The city centre around Anexartisias and Makariou Avenue has tight one-way systems, delivery vans, and constant pedestrian traffic, so good observation skills matter from day one. Move out toward Germasogeia and you get long straight roads with higher speeds, more roundabouts, and tricky merges onto the A1 motorway heading to Nicosia or Paphos. Traffic patterns in Limassol follow predictable rush hours. Mornings between 7:30 and 9:00 are heavy near schools and the port, while evenings between 4:30 and 6:30 fill up Spyrou Kyprianou, Franklin Roosevelt, and the seafront road. Most driving schools plan lessons around these peaks so learners get real traffic practice without being overwhelmed too early. Summer adds tourists, scooters, and rental cars to the mix, which is excellent training for handling the unexpected. Test routes typically run through Mesa Geitonia, Linopetra, and parts of Agios Athanasios, depending on which test centre you are assigned. Common test failures in Limassol come from rushed roundabout entries, weak mirror checks before lane changes, and poor parallel parking on a slope. A good local instructor will drill these skills until they are automatic. Road conditions are generally good, but watch for sudden potholes after winter rain and for slippery painted lines when wet. Limassol also has more roadworks than other cities because of constant construction near the marina and the new tower developments along the coast. Choosing a driving school that knows the current detours and temporary signs is a real advantage. The schools listed above all have strong local reputations and the experience to get you test-ready in 2026.

faq.q: How much do driving lessons cost in Limassol in 2026?
faq.a: Most Limassol driving schools charge between 25 and 35 euros per 45-minute lesson in 2026. Package deals for 10 or 20 lessons usually bring the price down. Always ask if the test car rental fee is included.

faq.q: How old do I have to be to start driving lessons in Cyprus?
faq.a: You can apply for a learner permit at 17 and a half and take the practical test from 18. Many Limassol schools accept students from 17 so they are ready to test on their 18th birthday.

faq.q: Do I need to pass a theory test before the practical test?
faq.a: Yes. You must pass the written theory test before booking your practical driving test in Cyprus. Most Limassol driving schools help students study and book the theory test through the Department of Road Transport.

faq.q: Can I learn to drive in English in Limassol?
faq.a: Yes. Many Limassol driving schools offer lessons in English, Greek, and sometimes Russian. This is helpful for the large expat and student community living in the city.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a driving licence in Limassol?
faq.a: Most students need between 15 and 25 practical lessons before they are ready to test. From your first lesson to holding a full licence usually takes 2 to 4 months, depending on test slot availability in 2026.
